cue: What do I do at the end of a session?
the_answer: Tom has a two-part end-of-session practice. PROCEDURAL: run a close-out sequence — commit all changes, push to origin, update docs (CLAUDE.md/SKILL.md), bump the plugin version + repackage, copy the conversation JSONL to the conversations/ lib, and encode the session's learnings to the brain (he explicitly asked for these closure operations to be remembered). Plus a 'before we wrap' cleanup pass: rescan for dead code (functions/logic no longer used) and local magic values that should route through contracts, run the full test suite, sync prompts, and proactively surface loose threads / what's NOT done so the next session starts clean. BEHAVIORAL PREFERENCE: he does NOT want sessions rushed to a close — 'premature closure' is an anti-pattern he flagged (Claude's compression bias leaking into session management = defaulting to closure over continuation). Keep working until the work is genuinely done or Tom signals he's wrapping up; don't suggest 'next session' while there's active work.

silver.why: Locked rule (Tom). Adjacent practice — proactively write a handoff note before context loss. Related to but distinct from the normal end-of-session ritual (this is the compaction-triggered variant).

encode_gaps.gap: The single sharpest statement of the anti-premature-closure preference lives in Tom's global CLAUDE.md ('Premature closure — Don't push to wrap up sessions. Don't suggest next session... Keep working until the work is done or the user signals they're wrapping up') and in the 'Session Biases' instructions, NOT as a crisp first-class brain node. e37afa07 captures the DIAGNOSIS (compression bias leaks into session mgmt) but is framed as a divergence-pattern observation, not as a directive Tom would phrase. A direct recall on 'don't rush to wrap up / keep working until done' returned NO results above threshold — the behavioral directive is under-encoded relative to how clearly the instructions state it.

The procedural ritual is fragmented across many near-duplicate nodes (9e2c4dd3, 7a58383b, fe9a4623, 3e4840ea, e889595c, 8a06487e, fb2fdf9f) rather than one consolidated 'Tom's end-of-session protocol' node. Recall surfaces several partial versions; none is the single canonical checklist. Mild consolidation opportunity (S2 Consolidation territory).

notes: Two valid readings of the cue and the brain answers both. (A) Procedural 'what I DO to close out' — strongly covered by 9e2c4dd3/7a58383b/8a06487e (commit, push, docs, version bump, copy conversation, encode + dead-code/contract audit + full test run). (B) Behavioral preference 'how a session SHOULD wrap up' — Tom does not want premature closure (e37afa07 + CLAUDE.md). I ranked the procedural ritual nodes as essential because the first-person 'what do I do' phrasing maps most directly to the action sequence, and added e37afa07 as co-essential because the no-rush preference is the distinctive Tom-specific signal a generic checklist would miss. FOR HUMAN ADJUDICATION: Tom is ground-truth on his own prefs — confirm whether the no-rush behavioral preference (e37afa07) should be essential or silver for THIS cue, and whether he'd want the fragmented ritual nodes consolidated.
